text:
alex: Heads up — main CI flipped red right after merge 0a7f3c. Failing stage: `smoke-infra-gpu` step `serve-sanity` timed out (10m). infra-bot posted the job link: https://ci.redwood/2450012345 :eyes:

infra-bot: CI failure summary: pipeline=main, build=2450012345, stage=smoke-infra-gpu, step=serve-sanity, status=TIMED_OUT (600s). Suggest rerun or bisect. Logs: `Connection timed out waiting for healthcheck`

priya: I merged a tiny revert earlier (PR #5234) but it only touched docs. cc @alex @jorge. Not expecting infra impact but pinging in case. :thinking_face:

jorge: I didn't touch the serving infra. Will grab logs. Can someone kick a rerun? if it passes then might be flake from infra autoscaler.

alex: @ci please rerun `smoke-infra-gpu` (or use the web UI). If rerun fails we should bisect.

sasha: Rerun started (job 2450012350). If we see the same error, check worker node allocation/taints. Past flake pattern: kube-scheduler was queuing GPU pods > 7m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

maya: Quick log snippet from the failing run:
```
2026-03-17T14:02:11Z serve: initializing container
2026-03-17T14:12:11Z serve: healthcheck timeout after 600s
2026-03-17T14:12:11Z serve: error: timed out waiting for tcp 127.0.0.1:8080
```
Looks like process never came up inside the pod. Could be image pull or startup hang.

jorge: Rerun (2450012350) is still failing with same timeout. I'll start a quick bisect across last two merges (0a7f3c..0b8d2a). Will try to repro locally with the smoke image.

priya: If you need me to revert my PR for quick mitigation I can do that, but I'd prefer to confirm it's related first.

alex: Thanks. If bisect shows a correlation, let's revert the offending commit and hotfix. For now tagging oncall: @sasha @maya. Also adding a temporary canary to route traffic off the new nodes until we're sure. :thumbsup:

jorge: Update: started bisect run 2450012450, running smoke container locally now. Will post results in this thread within ~20m.

sasha: Noted. If bisect fails to repro locally, please capture pod describe + kubelet logs from the CI worker: `kubectl describe pod <pod>` and `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200`. Post here.

alex: Appreciate it — keeping this thread as main triage.
